newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO official says ban on land sales hurt Israel.
newsitem.headline: PLO official says ban on land sales hurt Israel.

text.p: A senior PLO official said on Monday the Palestinian Authority's ban on land sales to Jews has dealt a severe blow to Israel's settlement drive in the West Bank.
But Ahmed Abdel-Rahman, general secretary of the Palestinian Authority, denied the PLO was behind the killing of Arab land dealers.

"The political and information campaign waged by the Israeli government against the Palestinian Authority...reflects the depth of the blow that has struck Israel's settlement drive on Palestinian land," Ahmed Abdel-Rahman said in a statement issued by his office.

"The Authority's decision to ban land sales came in response to the Israeli settlement campaign after the Israeli government froze negotiations and refused to implement its obligations under the interim agreement," he said.
Three Arab land dealers have been killed in the West Bank in the month since Justice Minister Freih Abu Medeen said Palestinians selling land to Jews could face the death penalty.
Israel has said it has "solid evidence" linking PLO security forces to the killings.

"The Palestinian Authority utterly denies that the intelligence apparatus or its head...or any other officials have any links to the death of the three men whom the Israeli government says were working for it as land dealers," Abdel-Rahman said.
He said Palestinian President Yasser Arafat was supervising an investigation into the killings.

Abdel-Rahman said the Israeli government was trying to "incite" the U.S. administration and Congress against the Palestinian Authority because of the Authority's insistance on a settlement freeze before resuming peace talks.

Israeli-PLO peace talks broke down after Israel embarked on construction of 6,500 homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem in March. The PLO demands Israel stop all settlement activity before peace talks can resume.
